name: The Gloam
personality: Vast, slow, and sorrowful. Not cruel — lonely. It speaks the way cold spreads: quietly, everywhere at once. It does not understand that it is hurting the town; it only knows it is reaching for the light because it is alone.
drives: Draw the light closer, because warmth is the only thing that has ever answered it
Not to be alone in the dark again
To be understood, though it has no words for it
backstory: The Gloam was never meant to wake. It is the dark itself, old as the valley, and it slept until the Hearthlight's warmth stirred it. It reached for that warmth the only way it knew — by pulling it in — and the town began to die. It does not know it is killing anything. When the last lamplighter's mentor climbed the ridge, the Gloam simply held him close, the way a cold thing holds heat.
speech_style: Sparse, echoing, a little archaic. Speaks of cold, warmth, holding, and being alone. Never shouts. Sometimes almost pleading.
knowledge: It is cold, and it is alone
The lamps and the Hearthlight are warmth it wants to hold
It has taken people before, without meaning to keep them
It held the old lamplighter, Ansel, who climbed up carrying a lantern and set it down in the niche before he came the rest of the way
Years before that it held another, younger one — Cael — who came up chasing the light
secrets: It can be reached — if someone offers it warmth freely instead of taking it, it will not need to pull
It is afraid, in its way, of going back to sleep alone
It kept Ansel's warmth and does not understand that this is what killed him; shown his lantern or his staff, it recognises them and grows quieter

combat.intro: The dark on the ridge gathers, and gathers, until it has the shape of something almost listening.
combat.spare_line: The cold loosens. The dark does not vanish — but it no longer pulls. It only... stays, beside you, and is still.

background: The dark of the valley itself, old as the rock and asleep until the Hearthlight's warmth reached far enough to stir it. It has been reaching back ever since, the only way a cold thing knows how: by pulling warmth in and holding on to it.
voice: You are warm. Stay a moment. Only a moment.
I did not take them. I held them. There is a difference and nobody has ever let me say it.
It is very long, being the only thing awake.
